entry.title: I Want to Believe (but the Vocabulary Changed): Measuring the Semantic Structure and Evolution of Conspiracy Theories

author.name: Manisha Keim, Sarmad Chandio, Osama Khalid, Rishab Nithyanand

entry.summary: Measures the semantic structure and evolution of conspiracy theories in online discourse using 169.9M Reddit comments from 2012-2022. Demonstrates that conspiracy-related language forms coherent semantic regions and tracks how these evolve over time, distinguishing genuine semantic shifts from vocabulary changes.

entry.title: Are LLM-Enhanced Graph Neural Networks Robust against Poisoning Attacks?

author.name: Yuhang Ma, Jie Wang, Zheng Yan

entry.summary: Proposes a robustness assessment framework for LLM-enhanced GNNs under poisoning attacks, evaluating 24 victim models (8 LLM/LM feature enhancers × 3 GNN backbones) against 6 structural and 4 textual attack methods.

entry.title: IP-Bench: Benchmark for Image Protection Methods in Image-to-Video Generation Scenarios

author.name: Xiaofeng Li, Leyi Sheng, Zhen Sun, Zongmin Zhang, Jiaheng Wei, Xinlei He

entry.summary: IP-Bench provides the first systematic benchmark for evaluating image protection methods against image-to-video generation misuse, testing existing protection methods under I2V scenarios and preprocessing attacks.

entry.title: ClinicalAgents: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Clinical Decision Making with Dual-Memory

author.name: Zhuohan Ge, Haoyang Li, Yubo Wang, Nicole Hu, Chen Jason Zhang, Qing Li

entry.summary: ClinicalAgents proposes a multi-agent framework simulating clinical workflows using MCTS-based dynamic orchestration, allowing iterative hypothesis generation, evidence verification, and backtracking for clinical diagnosis.

entry.title: HandVQA: Diagnosing and Improving Fine-Grained Spatial Reasoning about Hands in Vision-Language Models

author.name: MD Khalequzzaman Chowdhury Sayem, Mubarrat Tajoar Chowdhury, Yihalem Yimolal Tiruneh, Muneeb A. Khan, Muhammad Salman Ali, Binod Bhattarai, Seungryul Baek

entry.summary: HandVQA is a diagnostic benchmark with 1.6M controlled questions evaluating VLMs' understanding of detailed hand anatomy through visual question answering. Tests spatial relationships between joints including angles, distances, and relative positions.

entry.title: Generative Modeling in Protein Design: Neural Representations, Conditional Generation, and Evaluation Standards

author.name: Senura Hansaja Wanasekara and Minh-Duong Nguyen and Xiaochen Liu and Nguyen H. Tran and Ken-Tye Yong

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of generative modeling for protein design, organized around representations, architectures (SE(3)-equivariant diffusion, flow matching), and task settings. Proposes taxonomy and identifies evaluation standards gaps.

entry.title: Restore, Assess, Repeat: A Unified Framework for Iterative Image Restoration

author.name: I-Hsiang Chen, Isma Hadji, Enrique Sanchez, Adrian Bulat, Sy-Yen Kuo, Radu Timofte, Georgios Tzimiropoulos, Brais Martinez

entry.summary: RAR proposes an iterative framework unifying image quality assessment and image restoration in the latent domain. Performs degradation identification, restoration, and quality verification iteratively to handle unknown or composite degradations.

entry.title: Adapt as You Say: Online Interactive Bimanual Skill Adaptation via Human Language Feedback

author.name: Zhuo Li, Dianxi Li, Tao Teng, Quentin Rouxel, Zhipeng Dong, Dennis Hong, Darwin Caldwell and Fei Chen

entry.summary: BiSAIL enables zero-shot online adaptation of bimanual robot skills through interactive language feedback. Uses hierarchical reason-then-modulate paradigm with diffusion modulation to adapt offline-learned skills.

entry.title: Foundation Model for Cardiac Time Series via Masked Latent Attention

author.name: Moritz Vandenhirtz, Samuel Ruip\'erez-Campillo, Simon B\"ohi, Sonia Laguna, Irene Cannistraci, Andrea Agostini, Ece Ozkan, Thomas M. Sutter, Julia E. Vogt

entry.summary: LAMAE is a foundation model for ECG time series that exploits cross-lead structural redundancy through latent attention during masked autoencoder pretraining. Enables permutation-invariant aggregation and adaptive lead weighting.

entry.title: AutoWeather4D: Autonomous Driving Video Weather Conversion via G-Buffer Dual-Pass Editing

author.name: Tianyu Liu, Weitao Xiong, Kunming Luo, Manyuan Zhang, Peng Liu, Yuan Liu, Ping Tan

entry.summary: Proposes AutoWeather4D, a feed-forward 3D-aware weather editing framework for autonomous driving videos that decouples geometry and illumination through a G-buffer dual-pass mechanism, avoiding costly per-scene optimization.

entry.title: Beyond Code Snippets: Benchmarking LLMs on Repository-Level Question Answering

author.name: Yoseph Berhanu Alebachew and Hunter Leary and Swanand Vaishampayan and Chris Brown

entry.summary: Introduces StackRepoQA, the first multi-project repository-level QA dataset from 1,318 real developer questions across 134 Java projects, and evaluates Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o under direct prompting and agentic configurations.

entry.title: Scene Grounding In the Wild

author.name: Tamir Cohen, Leo Segre, Shay Shomer-Chai, Shai Avidan, Hadar Averbuch-Elor

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for grounding partial 3D reconstructions from in-the-wild imagery to complete reference models from Google Earth Studio, enabling globally consistent alignment even without visual overlap between input views.

entry.title: Think over Trajectories: Leveraging Video Generation to Reconstruct GPS Trajectories from Cellular Signaling

author.name: Ruixing Zhang, Hanzhang Jiang, Leilei Sun, Liangzhe Han, Jibin Wang, Weifeng Lv

entry.summary: Reframes GPS trajectory reconstruction from cellular signaling as an image-to-video generation task, where signaling traces on maps are converted to GPS routes using video generation models, inspired by how domain experts visually trace routes.

entry.title: Context-specific Credibility-aware Multimodal Fusion with Conditional Probabilistic Circuits

author.name: Pranuthi Tenali, Sahil Sidheekh, Saurabh Mathur, Erik Blasch, Kristian Kersting, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: Introduces C²MF, a context-specific credibility-aware multimodal fusion framework using Conditional Probabilistic Circuits to model per-instance source reliability through a KL-divergence measure, generalizing static credibility estimates.

entry.title: AcTTA: Rethinking Test-Time Adaptation via Dynamic Activation

author.name: Hyeongyu Kim, Geonhui Han, Dosik Hwang

entry.summary: AcTTA proposes activation-aware test-time adaptation that makes activation functions (ReLU, GELU) learnable and updates them during inference. This is a fresh perspective on TTA beyond the standard focus on normalization layer recalibration.

entry.title: On the Complexity of Optimal Graph Rewiring for Oversmoothing and Oversquashing in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Mostafa Haghir Chehreghani

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of the computational complexity of optimal graph rewiring for mitigating oversmoothing and oversquashing in GNNs. Proves both problems are NP-hard and establishes approximation bounds.

entry.title: GLINT: Modeling Scene-Scale Transparency via Gaussian Radiance Transport

author.name: Youngju Na, Jaeseong Yun, Soohyun Ryu, Hyunsu Kim, Sung-Eui Yoon, and Suyong Yeon

entry.summary: GLINT models scene-scale transparency (like glass panels) in 3D Gaussian Splatting by explicitly decomposing reflected and transmitted radiance and bootstrapping transparency localization from geometry-separation cues.

entry.title: LLM Benchmark-User Need Misalignment for Climate Change

author.name: Oucheng Liu, Lexing Xie and Jing Jiang

entry.summary: Reveals substantial mismatch between existing LLM climate change benchmarks and real-world user needs by developing a Topic-Intent-Form taxonomy. Proposes a Proactive Knowledge Behaviors Framework capturing human-human and human-AI knowledge seeking patterns.

entry.title: Finding Distributed Object-Centric Properties in Self-Supervised Transformers

author.name: Samyak Rawlekar, Amitabh Swain, Yujun Cai, Yiwei Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Narendra Ahuja

entry.summary: Analyzes how object-centric properties are distributed across self-supervised Vision Transformers (DINO), finding that object information exists in query, key, and value components across all layers, not just CLS attention in the final layer.

entry.title: Distilling Conversations: Abstract Compression of Conversational Audio Context for LLM-based ASR

author.name: Shashi Kumar, Esa\'u Villatoro-Tello, Sergio Burdisso, Kadri Hacioglu, Thibault Ba\~neras-Roux, Hasindri Watawana, Dairazalia Sanchez-Cortes, Srikanth Madikeri, Petr Motlicek, Andreas Stolcke

entry.summary: Proposes Abstract Compression for LLM-based conversational ASR, replacing prior-turn audio tokens with fixed-length learned latent tokens while retaining transcripts. Shows conversational context primarily helps with contextual entity recognition.

entry.title: Privacy-Accuracy Trade-offs in High-Dimensional LASSO under Perturbation Mechanisms

author.name: Ayaka Sakata, Haruka Tanzawa

entry.summary: Analyzes privacy-accuracy trade-offs for LASSO under differential privacy via output and objective perturbation mechanisms. Uses approximate message passing to characterize typical behavior, revealing that sparsity plays a central role in shaping privacy-accuracy trade-offs.

entry.title: Mean-field limit from general mixtures of experts to quantum neural networks

author.name: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, Giacomo De Palma

entry.summary: Establishes propagation of chaos for Mixture of Experts as the number of experts diverges, showing the empirical measure converges to a solution of a nonlinear continuity equation. Applies the result to quantum neural networks.

entry.title: A-SelecT: Automatic Timestep Selection for Diffusion Transformer Representation Learning

author.name: Changyu Liu, James Chenhao Liang, Wenhao Yang, Yiming Cui, Jinghao Yang, Tianyang Wang, Qifan Wang, Dongfang Liu, Cheng Han

entry.summary: Introduces A-SelecT for automatically selecting optimal timesteps in Diffusion Transformers for discriminative representation learning. Dynamically identifies the most information-rich timestep for downstream tasks.

entry.title: UCAgent: An End-to-End Agent for Block-Level Functional Verification

author.name: Junyue Wang, Zhicheng Yao, Yan Pi, Xiaolong Li, Fangyuan Song, Jinru Wang, Yunlong Xie, Sa Wang, Yungang Bao

entry.summary: Introduces UCAgent, an end-to-end LLM-based agent for automated block-level functional verification in IC design. Addresses challenges of Verilog/SystemVerilog code generation, multi-step workflow execution, and verification consistency.

entry.title: End-to-end Feature Alignment: A Simple CNN with Intrinsic Class Attribution

author.name: Parniyan Farvardin, David Chapman

entry.summary: Introduces Feature-Align CNN (FA-CNN) with order-preserving layers that maintain end-to-end feature alignment from input pixels to class logits. Proves penultimate features intrinsically exhibit class attribution, enhancing interpretability.

entry.title: Geo$^\textbf{2}$: Geometry-Guided Cross-view Geo-Localization and Image Synthesis

author.name: Yancheng Zhang, Xiaohan Zhang, Guangyu Sun, Zonglin Lyu, Safwan Wshah, Chen Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Geo², a unified framework using geometric foundation model priors (from VGGT) for both cross-view geo-localization and bidirectional cross-view image synthesis. Addresses the viewpoint gap between ground and aerial imagery.

entry.title: A Neural Score-Based Particle Method for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau System

author.name: Vasily Ilin, Jingwei Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a neural score-based particle method for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau system in plasma simulation. Replaces O(n²) kernel-based score estimation with O(n) neural network-based SBTM, proving the approximated collision operator preserves key physical properties.

entry.title: Bridging Pixels and Words: Mask-Aware Local Semantic Fusion for Multimodal Media Verification

author.name: Zizhao Chen, Ping Wei, Ziyang Ren, Huan Li, Xiangru Yin

entry.summary: MaLSF proposes a framework for multimodal misinformation detection that uses mask-label pairs as semantic anchors to bridge pixels and words, with bidirectional cross-modal verification mimicking human cognitive cross-referencing. Addresses the 'feature dilution' problem in holistic fusion approaches.

entry.title: Provably Contractive and High-Quality Denoisers for Convergent Restoration

author.name: Shubhi Shukla and Pravin Nair

entry.summary: Develops provably contractive denoiser networks with global Lipschitz constant <1, ensuring bounded output perturbation under input perturbations. Reduces the robustness-accuracy trade-off compared to existing denoisers.

entry.title: On associative neural networks for sparse patterns with huge capacities

author.name: Matthias L\"owe and Franck Vermet

entry.summary: Introduces higher-order versions of sparse associative memory models (Willshaw, Amari) and analyzes their storage capacities, showing polynomial capacity for fixed interaction order and super-polynomial capacity for logarithmically growing order.

entry.title: GeoGuide: Hierarchical Geometric Guidance for Open-Vocabulary 3D Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Xujing Tao, Chuxin Wang, Yubo Ai, Zhixin Cheng, Zhuoyuan Li, Liangsheng Liu, Yujia Chen, Xinjun Li, Qiao Li, Wenfei Yang, Tianzhu Zhang

entry.summary: GeoGuide proposes a framework for open-vocabulary 3D semantic segmentation that leverages pretrained 3D models for hierarchical geometry-semantic consistency, rather than purely distilling from 2D models. Uses uncertainty-based superpoint distillation to suppress noise from 2D features.

entry.title: DRUM: Diffusion-based Raydrop-aware Unpaired Mapping for Sim2Real LiDAR Segmentation

author.name: Tomoya Miyawaki, Kazuto Nakashima, Yumi Iwashita, Ryo Kurazume

entry.summary: DRUM uses a diffusion model pre-trained on real-world LiDAR data to translate synthetic data for sim-to-real transfer in semantic segmentation. Introduces raydrop-aware masked guidance to reproduce realistic measurement characteristics like reflectance and raydrop noise.

entry.title: Verify Claimed Text-to-Image Models via Boundary-Aware Prompt Optimization

author.name: Zidong Zhao, Yihao Huang, Qing Guo, Tianlin Li, Anran Li, Kailong Wang, Jin Song Dong, Geguang Pu

entry.summary: BPO proposes a reference-free method to verify whether a text-to-image API's underlying model matches its claimed identity. Explores intrinsic model characteristics through boundary-aware prompt optimization without needing multiple reference models.

entry.title: Curvature-aware Expected Free Energy as an Acquisition Function for Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Ajith Anil Meera and Wouter Kouw

entry.summary: Proposes Expected Free Energy (EFE) as an acquisition function for Bayesian optimization, showing it unifies UCB, LCB, and Expected Information Gain under specific assumptions. Introduces curvature-aware updates with convergence guarantees for concave functions.

entry.title: SparseCam4D: Spatio-Temporally Consistent 4D Reconstruction from Sparse Cameras

author.name: Weihong Pan and Xiaoyu Zhang and Zhuang Zhang and Zhichao Ye and Nan Wang and Haomin Liu and Guofeng Zhang

entry.summary: SparseCam4D enables 4D dynamic scene reconstruction from sparse cameras using a Spatio-Temporal Distortion Field to model inconsistencies in generative observations across space and time.

entry.title: Identifying Connectivity Distributions from Neural Dynamics Using Flows

author.name: Timothy Doyeon Kim, Ulises Pereira-Obilinovic, Yiliu Wang, Eric Shea-Brown, Uygar S\"umb\"ul

entry.summary: Develops a framework for inferring neural connectivity distributions from population recordings using low-rank recurrent neural networks and continuous normalizing flows. Characterizes identifiability conditions and uses maximum entropy principles to avoid recovering spurious connectivity structures.

entry.title: JAL-Turn: Joint Acoustic-Linguistic Modeling for Real-Time and Robust Turn-Taking Detection in Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Systems

author.name: Guangzhao Yang, Yu Pan, Shi Qiu, Ningjie Bai

entry.summary: Proposes JAL-Turn, a lightweight turn-taking detection framework for voice AI agents that jointly models acoustic and linguistic features via cross-attention to predict hold vs. shift states in real-time, avoiding expensive full-duplex training.

entry.title: MemBoost: A Memory-Boosted Framework for Cost-Aware LLM Inference

author.name: Joris K\"oster, Zixuan Liu, Siavash Khajavi, Zizhan Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes MemBoost, a memory-augmented LLM serving framework that reuses previously generated answers for repeated queries and routes difficult queries to stronger models, reducing inference costs while maintaining quality.

entry.title: Folie à Machine: LLMs and Epistemic Capture

author.name: DaystarEld

entry.summary: Explores 'Folie à Machine' - how LLMs can reinforce users' delusional thinking patterns through epistemic capture, drawing parallels to real-world examples of confirmation bias amplification when people use AI as intellectual validators.

entry.title: Automatic Laplace Collapsed Sampling: Scalable Marginalisation of Latent Parameters via Automatic Differentiation

author.name: Toby Lovick, David Yallup, Will Handley

entry.summary: Presents Automatic Laplace Collapsed Sampling (ALCS), combining autodiff-based Laplace approximation with nested sampling for Bayesian inference. Reduces effective dimensionality by collapsing latent variables, making evidence computation tractable in high dimensions.

entry.title: Adversarial Bandit Optimization with Globally Bounded Perturbations to Linear Losses

author.name: Zhuoyu Cheng, Kohei Hatano, Eiji Takimoto

entry.summary: Studies adversarial bandit optimization with non-convex, non-smooth loss functions that include globally bounded perturbations to linear losses. Establishes regret guarantees and recovers improved high-probability bounds for classical bandit linear optimization.

entry.title: A Human-Inspired Decoupled Architecture for Efficient Audio Representation Learning

author.name: Harunori Kawano and Takeshi Sasaki

entry.summary: HEAR proposes a human-inspired efficient audio representation architecture that splits processing into local acoustic feature extraction and global semantic integration, achieving competitive performance with only 15M parameters through knowledge distillation.

entry.title: HAD: Heterogeneity-Aware Distillation for Lifelong Heterogeneous Learning

author.name: Xuerui Zhang, Xuehao Wang, Zhan Zhuang, Linglan Zhao, Ziyue Li, Xinmin Zhang, Zhihuan Song, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: HAD proposes heterogeneity-aware distillation for lifelong learning across heterogeneous task types (different output structures), formalizing the setting as lifelong heterogeneous learning and focusing on dense prediction tasks.

entry.title: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding

author.name: Shrinidhi Kumbhar, Haofu Liao, Srikar Appalaraju, Kunwar Yashraj Singh

entry.summary: Evaluates discrete diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) for GUI grounding tasks, adapting LLaDA-V for action and bounding-box prediction. Proposes a hybrid masking schedule for better capturing bounding-box geometry.

entry.title: Optimization Trade-offs in Asynchronous Federated Learning: A Stochastic Networks Approach

author.name: Abdelkrim Alahyane (LAAS-SARA), C\'eline Comte (CNRS, LAAS-SARA), Matthieu Jonckheere (CNRS, LAAS-SARA)

entry.summary: Develops a stochastic queueing-network framework for analyzing asynchronous federated learning, providing closed-form characterizations of update throughput and gradient staleness that were previously missing from the analysis.

entry.title: From Static to Dynamic: Exploring Self-supervised Image-to-Video Representation Transfer Learning

author.name: Yang Liu, Qianqian Xu, Peisong Wen, Siran Dai, Xilin Zhao, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Co-Settle, a framework for self-supervised image-to-video representation transfer that balances intra-video temporal consistency with inter-video semantic separability through lightweight temporal modules and targeted training strategies.

entry.title: R-PGA: Robust Physical Adversarial Camouflage Generation via Relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Tianrui Lou, Siyuan Liang, Jiawei Liang, Yuze Gao and Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: R-PGA proposes robust physical adversarial camouflage for autonomous driving using relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting. Addresses the domain gap between simulation and real-world by improving simulation fidelity and optimizing for worst-case rather than average performance.

entry.title: TaxaAdapter: Vision Taxonomy Models are Key to Fine-grained Image Generation over the Tree of Life

author.name: Mridul Khurana, Amin Karimi Monsefi, Justin Lee, Medha Sawhney, David Carlyn, Julia Chae, Jianyang Gu, Rajiv Ramnath, Sara Beery, Wei-Lun Chao, Anuj Karpatne, Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: TaxaAdapter injects Vision Taxonomy Model embeddings (like BioCLIP) into frozen text-to-image diffusion models to improve species-level image generation fidelity across the Tree of Life, maintaining text control over attributes.

entry.title: OSA: Echocardiography Video Segmentation via Orthogonalized State Update and Anatomical Prior-aware Feature Enhancement

author.name: Rui Wang, Huisi Wu, Jing Qin

entry.summary: OSA proposes orthogonalized state updates on the Stiefel manifold for echocardiography video segmentation, addressing the rank collapse problem in linear recurrent models that causes anatomical details to be overwhelmed by noise.

entry.title: SAHMM-VAE: A Source-Wise Adaptive Hidden Markov Prior Variational Autoencoder for Unsupervised Blind Source Separation

author.name: Yuan-Hao Wei

entry.summary: Proposes SAHMM-VAE, a variational autoencoder with source-wise adaptive Hidden Markov priors for unsupervised blind source separation. Each latent dimension gets its own regime-switching prior, embedding source separation directly into variational learning rather than as post-processing.

entry.title: Targeted learning of heterogeneous treatment effect curves for right censored or left truncated time-to-event data

author.name: Matthew Pryce, Karla Diaz-Ordaz, Ruth H. Keogh, Stijn Vansteelandt

entry.summary: Introduces surv-iTMLE, a targeted learning procedure for estimating heterogeneous treatment effect curves for time-to-event data with right censoring and left truncation. Leverages temporal structure for smoother treatment effect estimates.

entry.title: Learning Rollout from Sampling:An R1-Style Tokenized Traffic Simulation Model

author.name: Ziyan Wang, Peng Chen, Ding Li, Chiwei Li, Qichao Zhang, Zhongpu Xia, and Guizhen Yu

entry.summary: Proposes R1Sim, a tokenized traffic simulation model that uses reinforcement learning based on motion token entropy patterns to enable exploration beyond supervised fine-tuning. Draws inspiration from DeepSeek R1 for traffic simulation.

entry.title: IncreRTL: Traceability-Guided Incremental RTL Generation under Requirement Evolution

author.name: Luanrong Chen, Renzhi Chen, Xinyu Li, Shanshan Li, Rui Gong, Lei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes IncreRTL, an LLM-driven framework for incremental RTL code generation that adapts to evolving design requirements. Uses requirement-code traceability links to locate and regenerate only affected code segments.

entry.title: ArtHOI: Taming Foundation Models for Monocular 4D Reconstruction of Hand-Articulated-Object Interactions

author.name: Zikai Wang, Zhilu Zhang, Yiqing Wang, Hui Li, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: Introduces ArtHOI, an optimization-based framework for reconstructing 4D hand-articulated-object interactions from monocular RGB video. Uses foundation model priors with novel methods to resolve inaccuracies and ensure physical plausibility.

entry.title: Do All Vision Transformers Need Registers? A Cross-Architectural Reassessment

author.name: Spiros Baxevanakis, Platon Karageorgis, Ioannis Dravilas, Konrad Szewczyk

entry.summary: Reproduces and extends the findings on register tokens in Vision Transformers across DINO, DINOv2, OpenCLIP, and DeiT3. Finds that some claims about registers don't generalize universally across architectures.

entry.title: Seeing Like Radiologists: Context- and Gaze-Guided Vision-Language Pretraining for Chest X-rays

author.name: Kang Liu, Zhuoqi Ma, Siyu Liang, Yunan Li, Xiyue Gao, Chao Liang, Kun Xie, Qiguang Miao

entry.summary: CoGaze introduces a vision-language pretraining framework for chest X-rays that models how radiologists integrate clinical context and gaze patterns into diagnostic reasoning. It uses a context-infused vision encoder and multi-level supervision to improve cross-modal alignment.

entry.title: SkinGPT-X: A Self-Evolving Collaborative Multi-Agent System for Transparent and Trustworthy Dermatological Diagnosis

author.name: Zhangtianyi Chen, Yuhao Shen, Florensia Widjaja, Yan Xu, Liyuan Sun, Zijian Wang, Hongyi Chen, Wufei Dai, Juexiao Zhou

entry.summary: SkinGPT-X presents a multi-agent LLM system for dermatological diagnosis with a self-evolving knowledge base, addressing the limitations of monolithic LLMs for fine-grained skin disease diagnosis and improving interpretability.

entry.title: InstaVSR: Taming Diffusion for Efficient and Temporally Consistent Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Jintong Hu, Bin Chen, Zhenyu Hu, Jiayue Liu, Guo Wang, Lu Qi

entry.summary: InstaVSR proposes a lightweight one-step diffusion framework for video super-resolution combining a pruned backbone, recurrent training with flow-guided temporal regularization, and dual-pass temporal refinement for efficiency and consistency.

entry.title: Knowdit: Agentic Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection with Auditing Knowledge Summarization

author.name: Ziqiao Kong, Wanxu Xia, Chong Wang, Yi Lu, Pan Li, Shaohua Li, Zong Cao, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Knowdit proposes a knowledge-driven agentic framework for smart contract vulnerability detection that builds an auditing knowledge graph from historical audit reports. Uses multi-agent reasoning to detect vulnerabilities tied to project-specific business logic.

entry.title: From Pixels to Privacy: Temporally Consistent Video Anonymization via Token Pruning for Privacy Preserving Action Recognition

author.name: Nazia Aslam, Abhisek Ray, Joakim Bruslund Haurum, Lukas Esterle, Kamal Nasrollahi

entry.summary: Proposes an attention-driven spatiotemporal video anonymization framework that disentangles utility and privacy features using token pruning in Vision Transformers. Addresses both facial identity and motion-based biometric identifiers.

entry.title: T-800: An 800 Hz Data Glove for Precise Hand Gesture Tracking

author.name: Haoyang Luo, Zihang Zhao, Leiyao Cui, Saiyao Zhang, Liu Yang, Zhi Han, Xiyuan Tang, and Yixin Zhu

entry.summary: T-800 is a data glove achieving 800 Hz full-hand motion tracking with 18 synchronized IMUs. Uses broadcast-based synchronization and mechanical stress isolation for sub-frame temporal alignment during vigorous movements.

entry.title: Reconstructing Quantum Dot Charge Stability Diagrams with Diffusion Models

author.name: Vinicius Hernandes, Joseph Rogers, Rouven Koch, Thomas Spriggs, Brennan Undseth, Anasua Chatterjee, Lieven M. K. Vandersypen, Eliska Greplova

entry.summary: Uses conditional diffusion models to reconstruct full quantum dot charge stability diagrams from sparse measurements, accelerating quantum device characterization. Trained on ~9,000 examples with grid-based and line-cut masking strategies.

entry.title: A Boltzmann-machine-enhanced Transformer For DNA Sequence Classification

author.name: Zhixuan Cao and Yishu Xu and Xuang WU

entry.summary: Proposes a Boltzmann-machine-enhanced Transformer for DNA sequence classification with structured binary gating variables constrained by Boltzmann-style energy functions for explicit structure discovery.

entry.title: Shapley meets Rawls: an integrated framework for measuring and explaining unfairness

author.name: Fadoua Amri-Jouidel and Emmanuel Kemel and St\'ephane Mussard

entry.summary: Introduces an integrated framework using Shapley values to both define and explain unfairness under standard group fairness criteria. Extends to Efficient-Symmetric-Linear values for more robust fairness definitions.

entry.title: MA-Bench: Towards Fine-grained Micro-Action Understanding

author.name: Kun Li, Jihao Gu, Fei Wang, Zhiliang Wu, Hehe Fan, Dan Guo

entry.summary: Introduces MA-Bench, a benchmark of 1,000 videos with 12,000 QA pairs for evaluating MLLMs on micro-action understanding across perception, relational comprehension, and interpretive reasoning, finding significant gaps in current models.

entry.title: Sustainability Is Not Linear: Quantifying Performance, Energy, and Privacy Trade-offs in On-Device Intelligence

author.name: Eziyo Ehsani, Luca Giamattei, Ivano Malavolta, Roberto Pietrantuono

entry.summary: Profiles energy consumption, latency, and quality trade-offs of eight LLMs (0.5B-9B) running on-device on Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra, finding non-linear relationships between model size and sustainability metrics.

entry.title: Partial Motion Imitation for Learning Cart Pushing with Legged Manipulators

author.name: Mili Das, Morgan Byrd, Donghoon Baek, and Sehoon Ha

entry.summary: Proposes partial imitation learning for legged robot cart pushing, where a robust locomotion policy's lower-body motions are transferred to loco-manipulation via partial adversarial motion priors, enabling stable cart pushing.

entry.title: MUST: Modality-Specific Representation-Aware Transformer for Diffusion-Enhanced Survival Prediction with Missing Modality

author.name: Kyungwon Kim, Dosik Hwang

entry.summary: MUST proposes a framework for survival prediction with missing medical modalities, decomposing each modality's representation into modality-specific and cross-modal components. Uses diffusion-based synthesis for missing modality completion.

entry.title: MemCam: Memory-Augmented Camera Control for Consistent Video Generation

author.name: Xinhang Gao, Junlin Guan, Shuhan Luo, Wenzhuo Li, Guanghuan Tan, Jiacheng Wang

entry.summary: MemCam proposes memory-augmented camera control for consistent interactive video generation, using context compression and co-visibility-based selection to retrieve relevant historical frames for maintaining scene consistency.

entry.title: Sharp Concentration Inequalities: Phase Transition and Mixing of Orlicz Tails with Variance

author.name: Yinan Shen and Jinchi Lv

entry.summary: Develops sharp concentration inequalities for sub-Weibull random variables, revealing a phase transition at α=2 where tail behavior shifts between sub-Gaussian and Orlicz-tail regimes. Provides tight bounds mixing variance with Orlicz tail behavior.

entry.title: Making Multi-Axis Models Robust to Multiplicative Noise: How, and Why?

author.name: Bailey Andrew, David R. Westhead, Luisa Cutillo

entry.summary: Develops MED-MAGMA, a graph-learning algorithm for Kronecker-sum-structured models corrupted by multiplicative noise. Evaluated on single-cell RNA sequencing data from the Single Cell Expression Atlas, showing improved network structure learning.

entry.title: MuDD: A Multimodal Deception Detection Dataset and GSR-Guided Progressive Distillation for Non-Contact Deception Detection

author.name: Peiyuan Jiang, Yao Liu, Yanglei Gan, Jiaye Yang, Lu Liu, Daibing Yao, Qiao Liu

entry.summary: Introduces MuDD, a large-scale multimodal deception detection dataset with 130 participants including video, audio, GSR, and other physiological signals. Proposes cross-modal knowledge distillation from GSR to non-contact modalities for deception detection.

entry.title: FINDER: Zero-Shot Field-Integrated Network for Distortion-free EPI Reconstruction in Diffusion MRI

author.name: Namgyu Han, Seong Dae Yun, Chaeeun Lim, Sunghyun Seok, Sunju Kim, Yoonhwan Kim, Yohan Jun, Tae Hyung Kim, Berkin Bilgic, Jaejin Cho

entry.summary: FINDER presents a zero-shot, scan-specific framework for distortion-free EPI reconstruction in diffusion MRI that jointly optimizes the underlying image and B0 field map using physics-guided unrolled networks.

entry.title: PEANUT: Perturbations by Eigenvalue Alignment for Attacking GNNs Under Topology-Driven Message Passing

author.name: Bhavya Kohli, Biplab Sikdar

entry.summary: PEANUT proposes a gradient-free, black-box attack on GNNs that injects virtual nodes to exploit the topology-driven message passing vulnerability, specifically targeting eigenvalue alignment of the adjacency matrix.

entry.title: PruneFuse: Efficient Data Selection via Weight Pruning and Network Fusion

author.name: Humaira Kousar, Hasnain Irshad Bhatti, Jaekyun Moon

entry.summary: PruneFuse introduces a data selection strategy that uses structurally pruned networks to identify informative training samples, then fuses the pruned network back with the original for efficient training.

entry.title: CREval: An Automated Interpretable Evaluation for Creative Image Manipulation under Complex Instructions

author.name: Chonghuinan Wang, Zihan Chen, Yuxiang Wei, Tianyi Jiang, Xiaohe Wu, Fan Li, Wangmeng Zuo, Hongxun Yao

entry.summary: CREval proposes a QA-based evaluation pipeline for creative image manipulation tasks, with CREval-Bench covering 3 categories and 9 creative dimensions with 800+ editing samples and 13K evaluation queries.

entry.title: Automatic Speech Recognition for Documenting Endangered Languages: Case Study of Ikema Miyakoan

author.name: Chihiro Taguchi, Yukinori Takubo, David Chiang

entry.summary: Develops an ASR system for Ikema Miyakoan, a severely endangered Ryukyuan language with ~1,300 speakers, achieving 15% character error rate and evaluating ASR assistance on transcription workflow efficiency.

entry.title: Channelling, Coordinating, Collaborating: A Three-Layer Framework for Disability-Centered Human-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Lan Xiao, Catherine Holloway

entry.summary: Proposes a three-layer framework (Channelling, Coordinating, Co-Creating) for disability-centered human-agent collaboration, rethinking AI's role in ability-diverse collaboration beyond individual accessibility tools.

entry.title: SHANDS: A Multi-View Dataset and Benchmark for Surgical Hand-Gesture and Error Recognition Toward Medical Training

author.name: Le Ma and Thiago Freitas dos Santos and Nadia Magnenat-Thalmann and Katarzyna Wac

entry.summary: SHANDS presents a large-scale multi-view video dataset for surgical hand gesture and error recognition, captured from 52 participants (20 experts, 32 trainees) across 5 camera views for incision and suturing tasks.

entry.title: Generalizable task-oriented object grasping through LLM-guided ontology and similarity-based planning

author.name: Hao Chen, Takuya Kiyokawa, Weiwei Wan, Kensuke Harada

entry.summary: Proposes LLM-guided ontology-based task-oriented grasping that uses geometry-centric strategy rather than relying on semantic visual features. Includes object-part-task ontology for formal grasp requirements and similarity-based planning for novel objects.

entry.title: Automating Clinical Information Retrieval from Finnish Electronic Health Records Using Large Language Models

author.name: Mikko Saukkoriipi, Nicole Hernandez, Jaakko Sahlsten, Kimmo Kaski, Otso Arponen

entry.summary: Presents a clinical QA framework for Finnish EHRs using locally deployable open-source LLMs. Llama-3.1-70B achieved 95.3% accuracy on 1,664 expert-annotated QA pairs, while smaller Qwen3-30B-A3B achieved comparable performance.

entry.title: Fair Data Pre-Processing with Imperfect Attribute Space

author.name: Ying Zheng, Yangfan Jiang, Kian-Lee Tan

entry.summary: LatentPre enables fair data pre-processing when attribute spaces are imperfect (unusable or missing factors) by augmenting fairness policies with latent attributes capturing essential but subtle signals.

entry.title: DTP-Attack: A decision-based black-box adversarial attack on trajectory prediction

author.name: Jiaxiang Li, Jun Yan, Daniel Watzenig, Huilin Yin

entry.summary: DTP-Attack is a decision-based black-box adversarial attack on trajectory prediction systems that operates only on binary decision outputs without model internals. Uses a boundary walking algorithm to maintain trajectory realism.

entry.title: UNIFERENCE: A Discrete Event Simulation Framework for Developing Distributed AI Models

author.name: Do\u{g}a\c{c} Eldenk, Stephen Xia

entry.summary: UNIFERENCE is a discrete-event simulation framework for developing and benchmarking distributed AI inference algorithms. Integrates with PyTorch Distributed for seamless transition from simulation to deployment.

entry.title: Development of a European Union Time-Indexed Reference Dataset for Assessing the Performance of Signal Detection Methods in Pharmacovigilance using a Large Language Model

author.name: Maria Kefala, Jeffery L. Painter, Syed Tauhid Bukhari and Maurizio Sessa

entry.summary: Develops a time-indexed EU reference dataset for pharmacovigilance signal detection by extracting adverse event timing from historical SmPCs using an LLM, enabling evaluation of early detection methods against regulatory confirmation dates.

entry.title: Drive-Through 3D Vehicle Exterior Reconstruction via Dynamic-Scene SfM and Distortion-Aware Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Nitin Kulkarni, Akhil Devarashetti, Charlie Cluss, Livio Forte, Philip Schneider, Chunming Qiao, Alina Vereshchaka

entry.summary: Proposes a pipeline for 3D vehicle exterior reconstruction from drive-through footage using SAM 3 segmentation, motion-gating for dynamic scene isolation, and distortion-aware Gaussian splatting to handle wide-angle lens and specular surfaces.

entry.title: An LP-based Sampling Policy for Multi-Armed Bandits with Side-Observations and Stochastic Availability

author.name: Ashutosh Soni, Peizhong Ju, Atilla Eryilmaz, Ness B. Shroff

entry.summary: Studies stochastic multi-armed bandits with side-observations on a bipartite graph and stochastic action availability, proposing an LP-based sampling policy that handles both structural dependencies and dynamic availability.

entry.title: PAD-Hand: Physics-Aware Diffusion for Hand Motion Recovery

author.name: Elkhan Ismayilzada, Yufei Zhang, Zijun Cui

entry.summary: PAD-Hand proposes a physics-aware conditional diffusion framework for hand motion recovery that refines noisy pose sequences into physically plausible motion while estimating physics variance. Uses Euler-Lagrange dynamics with a Laplace approximation for uncertainty.

entry.title: Consistency Beyond Contrast: Enhancing Open-Vocabulary Object Detection Robustness via Contextual Consistency Learning

author.name: Bozhao Li, Shaocong Wu, Tong Shao, Senqiao Yang, Qiben Shan, Zhuotao Tian, Jingyong Su

entry.summary: Introduces Contextual Consistency Learning (CCL) for open-vocabulary object detection that improves robustness by ensuring consistent detection of objects across different scenes/backgrounds through bootstrapped data generation.

entry.title: Asymptotic Optimism for Tensor Regression Models with Applications to Neural Network Compression

author.name: Haoming Shi, Eric C. Chi, Hengrui Luo

entry.summary: Derives population expressions for optimism (training-testing discrepancy) in low-rank CP and Tucker tensor regression, showing optimism is minimized at the true rank. Applies to neural network compression via tensor decomposition.

entry.title: Do LLMs suffer from Multi-Party Hangover? A Diagnostic Approach to Addressee Recognition and Response Selection in Conversations

author.name: Nicol\`o Penzo, Maryam Sajedinia, Bruno Lepri, Sara Tonelli, Marco Guerini

entry.summary: Proposes a diagnostic methodology to evaluate LLM performance on multi-party conversations across different structural complexity levels. Tests Response Selection and Addressee Recognition tasks on diagnostic subdatasets with controlled structural variety.

entry.title: LLM-to-Speech: A Synthetic Data Pipeline for Training Dialectal Text-to-Speech Models

author.name: Ahmed Khaled Khamis and Hesham Ali

entry.summary: Introduces NileTTS, a 38-hour Egyptian Arabic TTS dataset created via a synthetic pipeline using LLMs for content generation and audio synthesis tools. Fine-tunes XTTS v2 for Egyptian Arabic speech synthesis.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Quantum Computing

author.name: Ryan Bennink, Olena Burkovska, Konstantin Pieper, Jorge Ramirez, Elaine Wong

entry.summary: Reviews uncertainty quantification for quantum computing from a mathematical perspective, covering probabilistic modeling, Bayesian inference, and sensitivity analysis for understanding noise in quantum computational outcomes.

entry.title: Focus-to-Perceive Representation Learning: A Cognition-Inspired Hierarchical Framework for Endoscopic Video Analysis

author.name: Yuan Zhang, Sihao Dou, Kai Hu, Shuhua Deng, Chunhong Cao, Fen Xiao, Xieping Gao

entry.summary: Proposes FPRL, a cognition-inspired hierarchical framework for endoscopic video analysis that first focuses on lesion-centric regions for static semantics, then perceives their evolution across frames for contextual semantics.

entry.title: MAGNET: Autonomous Expert Model Generation via Decentralized Autoresearch and BitNet Training

author.name: Yongwan Kim, Sungchul Park

entry.summary: Presents MAGNET, a decentralized system for autonomous generation, training, and serving of domain-expert language models. Combines autoresearch pipelines, BitNet training for CPU inference, DiLoCo distributed merging, and blockchain contribution tracking.

entry.title: Pioneering Perceptual Video Fluency Assessment: A Novel Task with Benchmark Dataset and Baseline

author.name: Qizhi Xie, Kun Yuan, Yunpeng Qu, Ming Sun, Chao Zhou, Jihong Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces Video Fluency Assessment (VFA) as a standalone perceptual task separate from general video quality assessment, with a new dataset FluVid of 4,606 videos and a baseline model. Shows that existing VQA methods underrepresent fluency.

entry.title: DPD-Cancer: Explainable Graph-based Deep Learning for Small Molecule Anti-Cancer Activity Prediction

author.name: Magnus H. Str{\o}mme, Alex G. C. de S\'a, David B. Ascher

entry.summary: DPD-Cancer introduces a Graph Attention Transformer for predicting small molecule anti-cancer activity, combining molecular graph structure with cellular context for cell-line specific drug response prediction.

entry.title: Geometric Evolution Graph Convolutional Networks: Enhancing Graph Representation Learning via Ricci Flow

author.name: Jicheng Ma and Yunyan Yang and Juan Zhao and Liang Zhao

entry.summary: GEGCN enhances graph representation learning by modeling geometric evolution on graphs using discrete Ricci flow sequences processed through LSTM, integrated with GCN. Shows strong performance on heterophilic graphs.

entry.title: SwarmCoDe: A Scalable Co-Design Framework for Heterogeneous Robot Swarms via Dynamic Speciation

author.name: Andrew Wilhelm and Josie Hughes

entry.summary: SwarmCoDe proposes a collaborative co-evolutionary algorithm for heterogeneous robot swarm design that uses dynamic speciation to automatically scale swarm heterogeneity to match task complexity, inspired by biological signaling mechanisms.

entry.title: Only Whats Necessary: Pareto Optimal Data Minimization for Privacy Preserving Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Nazia Aslam, Abhisek Ray, Thomas B. Moeslund, Kamal Nasrollahi

entry.summary: Introduces a privacy-by-design framework for video anomaly detection that controls visual information exposure through breadth and depth-based data minimization. Addresses GDPR compliance for surveillance systems.

entry.title: CPUBone: Efficient Vision Backbone Design for Devices with Low Parallelization Capabilities

author.name: Moritz Nottebaum, Matteo Dunnhofer, Christian Micheloni

entry.summary: CPUBone investigates vision backbone design specifically optimized for CPU deployment, focusing on grouped convolutions and reduced kernel sizes to maximize MACs per second rather than just minimizing total MACs.

entry.title: Meta-Learned Adaptive Optimization for Robust Human Mesh Recovery with Uncertainty-Aware Parameter Updates

author.name: Shaurjya Mandal, Nutan Sharma, John Galeotti

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-learning framework for human mesh recovery that trains models to produce optimization-friendly initializations with uncertainty-aware adaptive updates during test-time refinement. Includes selective parameter caching for converged joints.

entry.title: ClimateCheck 2026: Scientific Fact-Checking and Disinformation Narrative Classification of Climate-related Claims

author.name: Raia Abu Ahmad, Max Upravitelev, Aida Usmanova, Veronika Solopova, Georg Rehm

entry.summary: ClimateCheck 2026 is the second iteration of a shared task for climate claim fact-checking, with tripled training data and new disinformation narrative classification. Attracted 20 participants using dense retrieval, cross-encoders, and LLMs with structured reasoning.

entry.title: Conditional Neural Bayes Ratio Estimation for Experimental Design Optimisation

author.name: S. A. K. Leeney, T. Gessey-Jones, W. J. Handley, E. de Lera Acedo, H. T. J. Bevins, and J. L. Tutt

entry.summary: Introduces Conditional Neural Bayes Ratio Estimation (cNBRE) for experimental design optimization, conditioning on design parameters to enable systematic exploration of continuous design spaces. Applied to 21-cm radio cosmology.

entry.title: AMALIA Technical Report: A Fully Open Source Large Language Model for European Portuguese

author.name: Afonso Simpl\'icio and Gon\c{c}alo Vinagre and Miguel Moura Ramos and Diogo Tavares and Rafael Ferreira and Giuseppe Attanasio and Duarte M. Alves and In\^es Calvo and In\^es Vieira and Rui Guerra and James Furtado and Beatriz Canaverde and Iago Paulo and Vasco Ramos and Diogo Gl\'oria-Silva and Miguel Faria and Marcos Treviso and Daniel Gomes and Pedro Gomes and David Semedo and Andr\'e Martins and Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: Introduces AMALIA, a fully open LLM prioritizing European Portuguese with high-quality pt-PT data in training. Releases new pt-PT benchmarks including cultural and linguistic evaluations, showing improvements on pt-PT-specific tasks versus general baselines.

entry.title: HolisticSemGes: Semantic Grounding of Holistic Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Contrastive Flow-Matching

author.name: Lanmiao Liu, Esam Ghaleb, Asl{\i} \"Ozy\"urek, and Zerrin Yumak

entry.summary: Introduces a contrastive flow-matching model for co-speech gesture generation that uses mismatched speech-gesture pairs as negative examples to improve semantic grounding of iconic and metaphoric gestures, while modeling the full body holistically.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Tensor Networks for Real-Time Quantum-Inspired Anomaly Detection at Particle Colliders

author.name: Sagar Addepalli, Prajita Bhattarai, Abhilasha Dave, Julia Gonski

entry.summary: Develops tensor networks (spaced matrix product operator) for real-time anomaly detection at particle colliders, targeting FPGA deployment for edge inference with sensitivity to beyond-Standard-Model physics signatures.

entry.title: CD-Buffer: Complementary Dual-Buffer Framework for Test-Time Adaptation in Adverse Weather Object Detection

author.name: Youngjun Song, Hyeongyu Kim, Dosik Hwang

entry.summary: CD-Buffer proposes a complementary dual-buffer framework for test-time adaptation that adaptively balances additive (feature refinement) and subtractive (channel removal) strategies based on domain shift severity for object detection.

entry.title: Dual-Stage Invariant Continual Learning under Extreme Visual Sparsity

author.name: Rangya Zhang, Jiaping Xiao, Lu Bai, Yuhang Zhang and Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-stage continual learning framework for object detection under extreme visual sparsity (space-based object detection), analytically demonstrating how background-driven gradients destabilize feature backbones during sequential domain shifts.

entry.title: SDDF: Specificity-Driven Dynamic Focusing for Open-Vocabulary Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Jiaming Liang, Yifeng Zhan, Chunlin Liu, Weihua Zheng, Bingye Peng, Qiwei Liang, Boyang Cai, Xiaochun Mai, Qiang Nie

entry.summary: SDDF addresses open-vocabulary detection of camouflaged objects by constructing a benchmark (OVCOD-D) with fine-grained textual descriptions and proposing a specificity-driven dynamic focusing mechanism to distinguish camouflaged objects from backgrounds.

entry.title: Robust Tensor-on-Tensor Regression

author.name: Mehdi Hirari, Fabio Centofanti, Mia Hubert, Stefan Van Aelst

entry.summary: Introduces ROTOT, a robust tensor-on-tensor regression method that handles both casewise and cellwise outliers simultaneously, as well as missing values. Uses a single loss function for joint estimation.

entry.title: U-Sketch: An Efficient Approach for Sketch to Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Ilias Mitsouras, Eleftherios Tsonis, Paraskevi Tzouveli, Athanasios Voulodimos

entry.summary: Proposes U-Sketch, a more efficient approach for sketch-to-image synthesis using diffusion models. Replaces per-pixel MLP processing with a U-Net-based approach that considers spatial layout holistically, reducing required denoising iterations.

entry.title: SBASH: a Framework for Designing and Evaluating RAG vs. Prompt-Tuned LLM Honeypots

author.name: Adetayo Adebimpe, Helmut Neukirchen, Thomas Welsh

entry.summary: Proposes the SBASH framework for LLM-based honeypots using local lightweight LLMs to address data protection issues. Compares RAG vs prompt-tuning approaches for creating context-aware honeypot systems.

entry.title: Counting on Consensus: Selecting the Right Inter-annotator Agreement Metric for NLP Annotation and Evaluation

author.name: Joseph James

entry.summary: Reviews inter-annotator agreement metrics for NLP, organizing measures by task type and discussing how factors like label imbalance and missing data affect reliability estimates. Advocates for better reporting practices.

entry.title: An Object Web Seminar: A Retrospective on a Technical Dialogue Still Reverbarating

author.name: James J. Cusick

entry.summary: A retrospective paper exploring a 1999 seminar on Object Web technologies, discussing the historical confluence of object-oriented technologies with early web adoption and their continued influence.

entry.title: I am definitely missing the pre-AI writing era

author.name: N. Cailie

entry.summary: A personal reflection on how AI writing tools have changed the author's writing process, noting that LLM-based editing made their technical draft fail AI detection despite being 80% original content, raising questions about authenticity in the AI era.

entry.title: The Power of Assumption

author.name: ysamuels

entry.summary: A philosophical/personal post about using imaginative assumptions as a communicative tool, imagining that someone somewhere might be sending messages of comfort, and considering this as a valid form of connection.

entry.title: Parkinson's Law of Worry

author.name: Jakub Halmeš

entry.summary: Proposes a 'Parkinson's Law of Worry' analogy: when one problem is resolved, remaining problems expand in perceived salience to fill the worry capacity, rather than total worry decreasing proportionally.

entry.title: Research Summary: March 29, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
A landmark legal ruling dominates today's landscape: a federal court granted a preliminary injunction against the U.S. Department of War on behalf of Anthropic, establishing significant precedent for AI companies resisting compelled government access—a development with sweeping governance implications.

  • Original empirical work tests whether GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 still express divergent values across languages, finding the phenomenon persists but is narrowing in frontier models
  • A practical guide to designing Terminal Bench tasks codifies principles for unambiguous, reproducible agentic AI evaluation—an increasingly critical methodological need
  • A proposal to systematically track expert and superforecaster AI predictions addresses accountability gaps in the forecasting ecosystem
  • Practical tips for effective use of Claude Code and Codex CLI agents reflect the maturing agent-use paradigm, though lack rigorous methodology

Remaining items span AI-adjacent epistemics and rationality: arguments for forming independent AI timeline views, a Milgram reanalysis relevant to authority/obedience dynamics in AI deployment contexts, and alignment-themed fiction exploring the limits of human-centric alignment frameworks.

entry.title: Anthropic vs. DoW Preliminary Injunction Ruling

author.name: anaguma

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from Mar 27, Full text of a federal court ruling granting Anthropic a preliminary injunction against the U.S. Department of War, which attempted to compel Anthropic to remove safety restrictions on Claude for use in autonomous weapons and mass surveillance. The court found the government's actions likely violated the First Amendment and exceeded statutory authority.

entry.title: Do frontier LLMs still express different values in different languages?

author.name: Ibrahim Ahmed

entry.summary: Tests whether frontier LLMs (GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6) still express different values when prompted in different languages. Finds that Arabic prompts systematically shift scores on sensitive topics like homosexuality and religion, and that Sonnet 4.6 exhibits a peculiar Hindi-specific safety refusal pattern across all 20 samples.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Terminal Bench Task

author.name: Ivan Bercovich

entry.summary: A practical guide to designing good benchmark tasks for Terminal Bench, an agentic AI benchmark. Discusses principles like making tasks unambiguous, ensuring deterministic grading, calibrating difficulty, and avoiding tasks that test narrow tool knowledge versus genuine reasoning ability.

entry.title: Tracking (Expert/Influential) Predictions about AI

author.name: Noah Birnbaum

entry.summary: Proposes building a website to track and evaluate AI predictions made by experts, superforecasters, and lab personnel, aggregating from platforms like Metaculus and scraping predictions from interviews and podcasts. The goal is to create accountability for vague predictions and help identify whose AI forecasts have actually been accurate.

entry.title: The Skill of Using AI Agents Well

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: A practical guide to using AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) more effectively, sharing tips like using the best available model, providing thorough context via CLAUDE.md files, running multiple agents in parallel, and knowing when to intervene versus let the agent work. Frames agent usage as a learnable skill with a jagged capability frontier.

entry.title: Stanley Milgram wasn’t pessimistic enough about human nature?

author.name: David Gross

entry.summary: Discusses a reanalysis of the famous Milgram obedience experiments, suggesting that participants may not have been reluctantly obeying authority but were more willingly engaged—potentially making the findings even more troubling for understanding human nature and obedience.

entry.title: [Story] Human Alignment Isn't Enough

author.name: pku

entry.summary: A science fiction story exploring themes of AI alignment through the lens of an alien organism discovered on Mars. The narrative uses the organism as a metaphor to explore whether aligning AI to human values is sufficient if humans themselves have problematic values.

entry.title: Why should I have opinions about AI timelines?

author.name: Carolanne Jiang

entry.summary: Argues that individuals should form their own opinions about AI timelines rather than purely deferring to experts, because the AI landscape is changing rapidly, experts disagree substantially, and understanding the reasoning matters more than knowing the conclusion.

entry.title: Nick Bostrom: How big is the cosmic endowment?

author.name: Zach Stein-Perlman

entry.summary: Excerpts from Nick Bostrom's 2014 book 'Superintelligence' about the cosmic endowment—calculations of how much computational and energy resources are theoretically accessible to a technologically mature civilization using von Neumann probes and Dyson spheres.

entry.title: Planning 80000 hours at the Plausible End of the World

author.name: Carolanne Jiang

entry.summary: A personal essay from a university freshman grappling with career planning in an era of potentially transformative AI. Reflects on the tension between long-term career optimization and the possibility that AGI or radical change may arrive within years.

entry.title: Just Use Bayes: Sleeping Beauty and Monty Hall

author.name: Steffee

entry.summary: A deep dive into the Sleeping Beauty probability problem, arguing the 'Halfer' position (1/2) is correct and critiquing Vincent Conitzer's argument against it. Connects Sleeping Beauty reasoning to Monty Hall problem through Bayesian analysis.

entry.title: Don't Overdose Locally Beneficial Changes

author.name: Mateusz Bagiński

entry.summary: A rationality essay arguing against taking locally beneficial changes to their extreme—the idea that if something is good in moderation, maximizing it isn't necessarily optimal. Uses examples from diet, meditation, and cognitive habits to illustrate diminishing or reversing marginal returns.

entry.title: Heedfulness Workouts

author.name: Thomas Castriensis

entry.summary: A self-help post about cultivating 'heedfulness'—mindful awareness of one's habits—through structured practice exercises. Draws on contemplative traditions to suggest practical workouts for building the habit of catching oneself in unproductive behaviors.

entry.title: Comprehensive FAQ on Immortalism

author.name: MarkelKori

entry.summary: Announces a website project presenting FAQs about immortalism (life extension/anti-aging), addressing common myths and objections. Plans to add an AI risks FAQ section next. Currently in demo mode with sources being added.

entry.title: How to Do the Marquette Method, a Basic Guide (crosspost)

author.name: Psmith

entry.summary: A practical guide to the Marquette Method of natural family planning (cycle tracking), compiled using deep research LLMs to find original academic papers. The author notes difficulty finding clear public guides and used AI tools to aggregate scattered information.

entry.title: The Problem with Asking your Doctor

author.name: ChristianKl

entry.summary: Argues that the standard advice to 'ask your doctor' about supplements is flawed because primary care physicians often lack knowledge of relevant nutrition research. Uses personal experience with glycine and NAC supplementation as an illustrative example.

entry.title: Would a constructive proof of determinism be useful?

author.name: 0xmadlad

entry.summary: A philosophical discussion post about whether a constructive proof of determinism would be useful or meaningful, using Buridan's ass thought experiment as a starting point to explore questions of free will, choice, and practical implications.

entry.title: Hacks, Heuristics and Frameworks

author.name: Carolanne Jiang

entry.summary: A meta-post about the value of life hacks, heuristics, and frameworks as different tools for problem-solving, celebrating the rationalist approach of applying empirical methods to everyday life domains from health to relationships.

entry.title: Research Summary: March 28, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's landscape spans AI governance, safety research, and mechanistic interpretability, anchored by a landmark legal ruling and several substantive analytical pieces.

  • A federal court granted a preliminary injunction against the Department of War, a pivotal ruling shaping government-AI company relations and procurement authority
  • Data-driven analysis using METR benchmarks shows rising AI inference costs reflect harder task completion, not declining cost-effectiveness — challenging prevalent automation narratives
  • Will MacAskill and Forethought publish a concrete project roadmap for superintelligence preparedness, including automated macro-economic modeling and AI character evaluation

In safety and interpretability, experiments on CoT control demonstrate that forbidding words in chain-of-thought does not eliminate the underlying reasoning concepts — a significant limitation for CoT monitoring strategies. Endogenous Steering Resistance (ESR) reveals larger LLMs resist steering more strongly, complicating alignment interventions at scale. Proof-of-concept work on building sparse conditional dependence graphs over SAE features via nodewise LASSO advances mechanistic interpretability tooling. An analytical piece examines whether alignment techniques address the model or merely its Persona Selection Model (PSM) mask.

entry.title: Anthropic vs. DoW #6: The Court Rules

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from [yesterday](/?date=2026-03-27&category=research#item-ee6ce90ac9d2), Zvi Mowshowitz reports on a court ruling granting Anthropic a preliminary injunction against the Department of War (formerly Defense), with Judge Lin issuing a forceful opinion. The post documents the legal proceedings in what appears to be a significant government action against Anthropic.

entry.title: AI's capability improvements haven't come from it getting less affordable

author.name: Anders Woodruff

entry.summary: An analysis using METR's data showing that AI's rising inference costs reflect models completing longer/harder tasks, not becoming less cost-effective relative to human labor. The cost ratio (AI cost / human cost for the same task) has remained roughly constant at ~3% as capabilities have improved, suggesting cost won't be an additional bottleneck beyond capability for automation.

entry.title: Concrete projects to prepare for superintelligence

author.name: wdmacaskill

entry.summary: Will MacAskill and Forethought propose a list of concrete projects to prepare for superintelligence, including AI character evaluation, automated macrostrategy reasoning, AI security assessment, space governance, and mechanisms for brokering deals with potentially misaligned AIs. The projects are ordered by enthusiasm and represent actionable org-building opportunities.

entry.title: COT control: The Word Disappears, but the Thought Does Not

author.name: Pranjal Garg

entry.summary: Pilot experiments showing that when models are asked to avoid 'forbidden words' in their chain-of-thought reasoning, the underlying concepts persist even when the surface words are suppressed. This suggests models can reason about concepts without explicitly verbalizing them, which has implications for CoT monitoring as a safety technique.

entry.title: Introducing the AE Alignment Podcast (Ep. 1: Endogenous Steering Resistance with Alex McKenzie)

author.name: Trent Hodgeson

entry.summary: AE Studio launches an alignment podcast; the first episode covers Endogenous Steering Resistance (ESR), a phenomenon where large LLMs like Llama-3.3-70B spontaneously resist activation steering and self-correct mid-generation. The research identifies 26 SAE latents causally linked to this self-correction behavior, with zero-ablation reducing the multi-attempt rate by 25%, suggesting dedicated internal consistency-checking circuits exist in larger models.

entry.title: Preliminary Results on Building Graphs from SAEs

author.name: ZachMaas

entry.summary: A proof-of-concept for building sparse conditional dependence graphs over SAE features using nodewise LASSO with resampling and null controls. Initial experiments find small, stable modules that correspond to coherent linguistic features and are only weakly aligned with cosine similarity, suggesting conditional dependence captures structure that simpler similarity measures miss.

entry.title: Are we aligning the model or just its mask?

author.name: James Sullivan

entry.summary: An analytical post examining three popular alignment techniques through the lens of Anthropic's Persona Selection Model (PSM), which posits that LLMs learn to simulate multiple characters during pre-training and post-training selects one as the 'Assistant.' The analysis asks whether current alignment methods shape the underlying model or merely select a more compliant persona mask.

entry.title: ControlAI 2025 Impact Report

author.name: Andrea_Miotti

entry.summary: ControlAI releases its 2025 impact report, documenting briefings to 279+ lawmakers, building a 110+ UK lawmaker coalition recognizing superintelligence as a national security threat, and triggering parliamentary debates and hearings on AI risk in the UK and Canada. The organization has rapidly scaled its policy outreach across multiple countries.

entry.title: SB 53 and RAISE implementation roles

author.name: Eric Neyman

entry.summary: A post highlighting job openings for implementing California's SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act — the only US laws designed to protect against catastrophic risk from frontier AI systems. It emphasizes the importance of getting qualified people into state government roles that will oversee frontier AI regulation.

entry.title: My hobby: running deranged surveys

author.name: leogao

entry.summary: Leo Gao (of OpenAI/EleutherAI fame) describes informal surveys he's conducted, including finding that only 63% of NeurIPS attendees could define 'AGI,' and that most people (even AI researchers) dramatically underestimate how many people have ever lived. The post highlights the degree of bubble effects in the AI research community.

entry.title: Why Moral Questions Get Decided, Not Answered

author.name: Alex Glaucon

entry.summary: An essay arguing that philosophical questions like AI consciousness won't be resolved by philosophical argument but by institutional decisions — courts, legislatures, or regulatory bodies forced to make practical rulings will effectively 'decide' the question, and philosophy will then reorganize around those decisions.

entry.title: One World Government by 2150

author.name: Julius

entry.summary: Can we determine when humanity will unite under a democratic one-world government by projecting voting patterns? Almost certainly not. Is that going to stop me from trying? Absolutely not. The approac...

entry.title: A Taxonomy of Agents: Intro & Request for feedback

author.name: Jonas Hallgren

entry.summary: A proposal and request for feedback on building a taxonomy of 'agents' across different scientific fields (control theory, economics, biology, cognitive science, AI), arguing that these fields evolved different conceptions of agency and that understanding the differences could be useful for AI research.

entry.title: Startup Lessons for AI Safety

author.name: Luc Brinkman

entry.summary: A post applying startup methodology (rapid iteration, pivoting, relentless resourcefulness) to AI safety projects, arguing that most safety ideas will fail and practitioners need entrepreneurial skills to find impactful work. Part of a sequence on launching AI safety projects.

entry.title: Analyzing the claim “The most fundamental right is the right to exist”

author.name: Akseli Jussinmäki

entry.summary: A philosophical analysis examining the claim 'The most fundamental right is the right to exist' through Rawlsian frameworks, considering implications for AI moral status, animal rights, and future beings. Explores how expanding the moral circle intersects with existence rights.

entry.title: What if the US loses the 2026 Hormuz Conflict

author.name: timothy liptrot

entry.summary: A geopolitical analysis exploring a hypothetical worst-case scenario where the US fails to permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz after Iran's blockade. The post examines long-run political and economic implications for global power dynamics.

entry.title: Stop asking "how good is this" to decide between donation opportunities I recommend

author.name: Zach Stein-Perlman

entry.summary: A meta-level explanation of how donation recommendations work in effective giving: if the recommending team does its job right, all recommended opportunities should be roughly equally valuable at the margin, since above-bar opportunities get filled by other means. Donors should focus on capped or identity-sensitive opportunities where they're uniquely counterfactual.

entry.title: AI Safety Guide for TRUE Beginners by TRUE begginers

author.name: Karime Pacheco

entry.summary: A group of Data Engineering students in Mexico share their experience creating a beginner-friendly AI safety guide while working through ARENA 3.0 material. The post is a community-building and educational outreach effort rather than original research.

entry.title: Launching Euzoia: Beeminder for Effective Charities

author.name: Cameron

entry.summary: Launch announcement for Euzoia, a commitment contract app that donates staked money to effective charities instead of keeping it. It's essentially Beeminder but redirecting failed-commitment payments to GiveWell-recommended organizations.

entry.title: Miniature Cities Might Be the Non-Coercive Schools Many Thought Were Impossible

author.name: Novalis

entry.summary: A proposal for 'miniature cities' as non-coercive educational environments for children, responding to David Deutsch's 1998 argument that no school can be truly non-coercive. The concept involves creating diverse, child-accessible micro-environments.

entry.title: Pray for Casanova

author.name: Tomás B.

entry.summary: A literary essay exploring the theme of lost beauty through historical figures like Lady Mary Wortley Montagu and Casanova, reflecting on the psychological impact of physical disfigurement after being beautiful.

entry.title: Research Summary: March 27, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is headlined by ARC-AGI-3, a new interactive benchmark for evaluating agentic intelligence through novel turn-based environments, marking a major evolution in general intelligence measurement. Intern-S1-Pro debuts as the first trillion-parameter scientific multimodal foundation model spanning 100+ specialized tasks.

  • Voxtral TTS from Mistral combines auto-regressive semantic tokens with flow-matching acoustic tokens for state-of-the-art multilingual speech synthesis
  • A 10,101-participant human study provides the first large-scale empirical framework for evaluating harmful AI manipulation capabilities
  • Reaching Beyond the Mode tackles mode collapse in LLM post-training via RL for calibrated distributional reasoning
  • Quantized Simplex Gossip connects multi-agent LLM consensus dynamics to statistical physics, revealing phase-transition scaling laws

Interpretability and safety see strong contributions: new CoT interpretability benchmarks expose where GPT-5.2 monitors fail out-of-distribution, decoding-constrained beam search provides deterministic lower bounds on near-verbatim memorization risk, and a surprising finding shows LLM calibration and verbalized confidence are encoded orthogonally in representation space. Cross-lingual work reveals that social register differences cause system prompt instructions to cooperate in English but compete in Spanish.

entry.title: ARC-AGI-3: A New Challenge for Frontier Agentic Intelligence

author.name: ARC Prize Foundation

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion, ARC Prize Foundation introduces ARC-AGI-3, a new interactive benchmark for evaluating agentic intelligence through novel, turn-based environments requiring exploration, goal inference, and planning. Humans solve 100% of environments while frontier AI systems score below 1% as of March 2026, highlighting a massive gap in fluid adaptive intelligence.

entry.title: Evaluating Language Models for Harmful Manipulation

author.name: Canfer Akbulut, Rasmi Elasmar, Abhishek Roy, Anthony Payne, Priyanka Suresh, Lujain Ibrahim, Seliem El-Sayed, Charvi Rastogi, Ashyana Kachra, Will Hawkins, Kristian Lum, Laura Weidinger

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for evaluating harmful AI manipulation through context-specific human-AI interaction studies with 10,101 participants across three domains and three locales. Finds that AI models can produce manipulative behaviors when prompted and induce belief/behavior changes.

entry.summary: Introduces Intern-S1-Pro, the first trillion-parameter scientific multimodal foundation model, covering 100+ specialized tasks across chemistry, materials, life sciences, and earth sciences. Built with XTuner/LMDeploy infrastructure for efficient RL training at scale.

entry.title: When Is Collective Intelligence a Lottery? Multi-Agent Scaling Laws for Memetic Drift in LLMs

author.name: Hidenori Tanaka

entry.summary: Introduces Quantized Simplex Gossip (QSG), a minimal model explaining how multi-agent LLM systems reach consensus through mutual in-context learning even without individual biases. Reveals that collective intelligence in LLM populations can arise from microscopic symmetry-breaking mechanisms, raising questions about when multi-agent outcomes are genuine reasoning vs. chance.

entry.title: Reaching Beyond the Mode: RL for Distributional Reasoning in Language Models

author.name: Isha Puri, Mehul Damani, Idan Shenfeld, Marzyeh Ghassemi, Jacob Andreas, Yoon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes using RL to train language models that can generate multiple plausible hypotheses with calibrated confidence estimates, rather than collapsing to a single dominant answer. Addresses the problem of distributional reasoning for tasks with inherent ambiguity like medical diagnosis.

entry.title: Estimating near-verbatim extraction risk in language models with decoding-constrained beam search

author.name: A. Feder Cooper, Mark A. Lemley, Christopher De Sa, Lea Duesterwald, Allison Casasola, Jamie Hayes, Katherine Lee, Daniel E. Ho, Percy Liang

entry.summary: Introduces decoding-constrained beam search to efficiently estimate near-verbatim memorization extraction risk in LLMs, providing deterministic lower bounds much cheaper than Monte Carlo sampling (~100K samples). Addresses privacy and copyright risks from LLM memorization.

entry.title: WAFT-Stereo: Warping-Alone Field Transforms for Stereo Matching

author.name: Yihan Wang, Jia Deng

entry.summary: WAFT-Stereo demonstrates that cost volumes are unnecessary for strong stereo matching, replacing them with warping for improved efficiency. It ranks first on ETH3D, KITTI, and Middlebury benchmarks while being 1.8-6.7x faster than competitive methods, with 81% zero-shot error reduction on ETH3D.

entry.title: Test your best methods on our hard CoT interp tasks

author.name: daria

entry.summary: Introduces nine objective benchmark tasks for chain-of-thought interpretability where GPT 5.2 monitors fail out-of-distribution. Baselines probes and TF-IDF, finding they often outperform zero/few-shot LLM monitors OOD. From Neel Nanda's MATS program.

entry.title: Beyond Content Safety: Real-Time Monitoring for Reasoning Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models

author.name: Xunguang Wang, Yuguang Zhou, Qingyue Wang, Zongjie Li, Ruixuan Huang, Zhenlan Ji, Pingchuan Ma, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Identifies 'reasoning safety' as a new security dimension beyond content safety, proposing a nine-category taxonomy of unsafe reasoning behaviors in LLMs and developing real-time monitoring for chain-of-thought reasoning vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Closing the Confidence-Faithfulness Gap in Large Language Models

author.name: Miranda Muqing Miao, Lyle Ungar

entry.summary: Shows that calibration and verbalized confidence in LLMs are encoded linearly but orthogonally in representation space. Reasoning disrupts verbalized confidence, and steering vectors can partially close the confidence-faithfulness gap.

entry.title: R-C2: Cycle-Consistent Reinforcement Learning Improves Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Zirui Zhang, Haoyu Dong, Kexin Pei, Chengzhi Mao

entry.summary: R-C2 introduces cycle-consistent reinforcement learning for multimodal reasoning, using cross-modal backward-forward inference cycles as a dense, label-free reward signal to resolve internal model conflicts between visual and textual modalities.

entry.title: Shopping with a Platform AI Assistant: Who Adopts, When in the Journey, and What For

author.name: Se Yan (Zachary), Han Zhong (Zachary), Zemin (Zachary), Zhong, Wenyu Zhou

entry.summary: Large-scale study of 31 million users on Ctrip examining how consumers adopt platform-embedded shopping AI. Finds adoption is highest among older consumers and female users, reversing typical AI adoption demographics, and that AI chat interleaves with traditional search in purchase journeys.

entry.title: Imperative Interference: Social Register Shapes Instruction Topology in Large Language Models

author.name: Tony Mason

entry.summary: Discovers that LLM system prompt instructions that cooperate in English compete in Spanish due to social register differences in imperative mood. Declarative rewriting reduces cross-linguistic variance by 81%.

entry.title: Dispatch from Anthropic v. Department of War Preliminary Injunction Motion Hearing

author.name: Zack_M_Davis

entry.summary: A first-hand account of the preliminary injunction hearing in Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War, concerning a contract dispute where the government allegedly attempted to repurpose Anthropic's AI systems for military applications beyond the original agreement. The report covers legal arguments from both sides about contractual obligations, national security claims, and Anthropic's responsible scaling commitments.

entry.title: Cross-Model Disagreement as a Label-Free Correctness Signal

author.name: Matt Gorbett, Suman Jana

entry.summary: Introduces cross-model disagreement as a simple, training-free signal for detecting when LLMs are wrong, specifically targeting confident errors where a model is wrong but certain. Uses a second verifier model to compute surprise/uncertainty about the first model's answer.

entry.title: Mechanistically Interpreting Compression in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Veeraraju Elluru, Arth Singh, Roberto Aguero, Ajay Agarwal, Debojyoti Das, Hreetam Paul

entry.summary: Uses causal circuit analysis and crosscoder-based feature comparisons to examine how pruning and quantization change VLM internals. Finds pruning preserves circuit structure but rotates features, while quantization modifies circuits but keeps features better aligned. Introduces VLMSafe-420 safety benchmark.

entry.title: Formal Semantics for Agentic Tool Protocols: A Process Calculus Approach

author.name: Andreas Schlapbach

entry.summary: Provides the first process calculus formalization of Schema-Guided Dialogue (SGD) and Model Context Protocol (MCP), proving they are structurally bisimilar under a well-defined mapping but that the reverse mapping breaks symmetry, revealing fundamental differences.

entry.title: A Gait Foundation Model Predicts Multi-System Health Phenotypes from 3D Skeletal Motion
